1.Development Description of FPGA
1.1 Introduction of on-board FPGA configuration

SEA on-board FPGA uses Xilinx's Spartan-7 Series xc7s15ftgb196-1, and the FPGA chip is shown in the figure
below:

The resource configuration of chip is as follows:
• 12800 logic cells, 2000 slices, each containing 4 6-input LUTs and 8 flip-flops (total of 8,000
LUTs and 16,000 flip-flops)

• 150Kb of distributed RAM

• 20 DSP48E cells

• 10 blocks of 36Kb/20 blocks of 18Kb BRAM (total storage capacity of 360Kb)

• 2 clock management cells, each containing a MMCM and PLL

• 100 Max. user I/O number

Other off-chip configurations are as follows:
• Equipped with universal video Mini HDMI output interface, universal camera MIPI interface, AD/DA conversion
chip, 6-axis sensor
• Equipped with 2 ordinary LEDs, 2 cascaded RGB LEDs, 3 programmable buttons
• With 10 expansion IO ports, 14 Arduino compatible ports
• Equipped with 6-wire JTAG download interface

1.3 Description of on-board FPGA interface

1.3.1 LED of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

On-board LED has two general LEDs and two RGB LEDs.
Note:
• RGB LED is driven by SK6805 Series chips, which can be cascaded in multiple stages for display
development

• Provide basic routines such as LED breathing light, RGB LED breathing light, LED blinking, etc.

1.3.2 Mini HDMI of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

The Mini HDMI interface has the same signal interface mode except its size is smaller than HDMI interface. At
present, the specific support of on-board HDMI interface is as follows:

• Support basic functions such as video output, programmable HDMI hot plug, EDID recognition, etc.
• Do not support DCC multi-channel selection (selected by default)

The official case provides HDMI-driven display cases, including color bar display, checkerboard, pictures, etc.,
using Digilent's rgb2dvi interface IP (cannot transmit audio, only supports 24-bit RGB data transmission).

1.3.3 MIPI camera of on-board FPGA peripheral interface
Unlike other OV Series interfaces, the MIPI interface on the SEA board is 15pin, which is an industrial-grade camera
interface (the MIPI CSI interface used by mobile phones and Raspberry Pi cameras).Currently, it supports the
following:

• Default IIC to initialize the MIPI camera (the initial communication method cannot be changed)
• Camera access, support OV5647 camera, 720p@60Hz


The official case provides the driver of the OV5647 camera and the basic cases of image processing, including
camera image display, edge detection, HSV spatial domain transformation, color tracking, shape
recognition, etc.

1.3.4 Gyro of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

The board is equipped with a 6-axis sensor chip LSM6DS3TR, which can read posture data. The specific support
is as follows:

• The Gyro is hung on the IIC bus (FPGA_ESP_SDA, FPGA_ESP_SCL), FPGA and ESP32 can read the
posture data
• The Gyro supports reading of temperature, angle, angular velocity, and magnetometer
data

The official case provides the driver of LSM6DS3TR gyro, including initial configuration (setting filter parameters,
reading order, etc.), temperature, angle, angular velocity data reading and forwarding, etc.

1.3.5 ADC of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

The board is equipped with the ADC1173 module, which can read analog signals. The specific support is as follows:

• ADC1173 is a low-power consumption, 15MSPS analog-to-digital converter, output 8-bit digital signal,
power consumption only 33mW (typical value)

• The clock for analog-to-digital conversion is provided by an external clock (pin provided by
FPGA), ranging from 1MHz to 20MHz, of which the conversion effect is best at 15MHz.

Official case provides ADC1173 driver, including ADC sampling and waveform indicator

1.3.6 DAC of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

The board is equipped with the DAC7311 module, which can output analog signals.The specific support is as follows:

• DAC7311 is a 12bit, low power consumption, single channel, digital to analog conversion chip of voltage
output

• Use a universal three-wire serial communication interface with a clock frequency of up to 50MHz,
compatible with standard SPI, QSPI, and digital signal processor (DSP) interfaces.

Official case provides DAC7311 driver, and signal generator cases,etc

1.3.7 Buttons of on-board FPGA peripheral interface

The board has three user-programmable buttons, the default is high level, usually the black FPGA_RST is used as
the reset button, low level reset

1.3.8 Arduino compatible IO interface of on-board FPGA interface
The board has 18 Arduino compatible IO interfaces, which can be directly extended with Arduino, or use its
supporting peripherals, or develop by yourself. At present, the official support is as follows:

• Provide SPI communication example between Arduino and FPGA

• Provide digital extension daughter board, joystick extension daughter board, etc., and attach with
corresponding driving examples such as flowing water light, digital tube, joystick, Bluetooth, etc.

1.3.9 FPGA expansion IO interface of on-board FPGA interface

In the case of making full use of FPGA IO, the remaining 10 FPGA IO are reserved and connected to terminals to form
FPGA_IO0—FPGA_IO9 has 10 expansion IO in total, which can be programmed and developed by yourself and
connected with peripherals,etc

Map HDMI, MIPI, ADC/DAC, Arduino headers to FPGA pins from the manual.

对照手册引脚表，弄清 HDMI、MIPI、ADC/DAC、Arduino 口对应 FPGA 脚位。
在实验台「板子」页点亮本课相关功能块，和原理图概念对齐。

2. Front Installation Description of FPGA
2.1 JTAG downloader

The board is equipped with a JTAG download interface to facilitate programming and debugging, but because the
Flash is not directly mounted, the program cannot be solidified.The position of the JATG interface is shown in the
figure below, and the 6-wire interface (VREF, GND, TMS, TCK, TDO, TDI ) is used.

JTAG downloader, as shown in the figure below (one with adapter board, one without):

For the JTAG downloader without an adapter board, it needs to be connected to the board through a DuPont line.
Please judge the connection method according to the prominent position. Pay attention to the following points when
connecting with DuPont line:
• The DuPont line is easy to loosen, and sometimes it needs to be pressed by hand, otherwise JTAG cannot
recognize the board
• Sometimes, it is necessary to connect 2-3 ground wires from JTAG to the board
• When the above two conditions can not be recognized, you need to switch K1 of the DIP switch to ON
mode
• When the above three conditions can not be recognized, please check whether the JTAG wiring is correct

Taking into account the problem of adapter board, the PCB Geber Files (in the attachment package) of the adapter
board are provided, which can be used for board-making and welding. The three views of the adapter board and
the actual wiring are as follows:

2.2 Additional peripherals

2.2.1 MIPI interface camera of additional peripherals

The board has a MIPI camera interface. The official routine only provides the MIPI camera of OV5647. Here is the
physical map of the MIPI OV5647 camera (for reference only, some purchases may be different, such as bare feet,
infrared, etc.) and physical wiring diagrams.

If you want to test whether the wiring is correct or the contact is good, please program the bit file in the camera case.
After 10-20 seconds, the back of the camera will feel warm, indicating that the camera is in good contact and working
normally.

2.2.2 Display screen of additional peripherals

The board has a Mini HDMI interface, and an HDMI display case is provided in the official case, which requires a
display screen.

For the display screen, HDMI, VGA, DP, DVI and other interfaces can be used, and must support 1080p (Note:
Supporting 1080p does not necessarily support 720p, and household TV generally support 1080p).

For different interfaces of the display screen, different Mini HDMI adapter cables are required. Normally, the HDMI
interface display screen is more common, and Mini HDMI to HDMI cable is more common (no hardware circuit
conversion, only interface size, male and female connector conversion).

Therefore, it is recommended to use HDMI interface display screen, and equipped with mini HDMI to HDMI adapter
cable.

goal_en:

procedure:
3. Description of FPGA Development Platform
FPGA programming and development are divided into multiple EDA platforms according to different FPGA chips.
SEA on-board FPGA uses Xilinx's Spartan-7 Series chips, the development platform is Vivado 2018.2, which is
oriented to teaching and compatible with multiple operating systems.

3.1 Configuration of Vivado development environment

The specific configuration process is as follows:

(1) First,Open Xilinx official website, find technical support, select Vivado, select the version 2018.2(also can
select 2018.3)

(2) Considering the download speed, you can download it through other methods (such as Baidu cloud disk, etc.)

(3) After the download is complete, an iso file or tar file named Xilinx_Vivado_SDK_2018_2 will be obtained. Please
pay attention to the following two points:
• iso file: After unzipping directly, an error may be reported during installation. It is best to use Daemol Tools to
directly open the iso file for installation
• tar file: need to be unzipped in Linux environment, or use 7-Zip software to unzip

(4) After unzipping is complete, the folder is as follows:

(5) Run the xsetup.exe file (you need to run as an administrator and allow the firewall settings in the pop-up
window), and then enter the installation waiting status.The waiting time depends on the location of the installation
package, and the time is sorted from long to short: mechanical hard disk ( USB external)>SSD (USB external)/U
disk>PC internal mechanical hard disk>PC internal solid-state hard disk

(6) Then enter the following installation interface, and Get Latest Version will pop up. Click continue, and then Next.

(7) Check three Agree, and then click Next.

(8)You can check 1 or 2, among which 1 means free version, and you can apply for license through Xilinx official
website, and 2 means paid version (or has license). The devices and IDE covered are comprehensive. Please select
according to your personal situation.

(9)Then check the device according to the requirements.

(10) Then select the installation location, click Next, and then click Finish
Where, the following points need to be paid attention:

• The installation location can be customized
• It is recommended not to install on the C drive (occupies a large space)
• It is recommended to install on a solid state drive (fast boot)
(11) During the installation, USB related drivers (JTAG, etc.) will automatically pop up and must be installed

(12) After the installation is complete, the License Manager will pop up automatically, click Load License->Copy
License, and select your own License file. If the license file is satisfied, the environment configuration is completed.

3.2 Introduction of use for Vivado IDE

3.2.1 Introduction of start interface
Run Vivado IDE software and enter the following initial interface.

(1)The initial interface includes two parts, including the upper toolbar and the shortcut interface.
(2) In the toolbar:
•
In File, you can open project, create project, add IP location, and exit IDE
•
You can open Static Simulation files and open the JTAG connection interface (Open HardWare) in Flow
•
Tools can run TCL, Compile Simulation Libraries, grammar module constraints and other templates as well as Vivado
setting
•
You can open the Tcl Concole interface in Window and run Tcl command
•
You can view related information, License Manager, etc. in Help

(3) In the shortcut interface:

•
Project creation, project opening, and sample project opening can be performed in Quick Start
•
In Tasks, you can open IP management, open JTAG connection interface (Open HardWare), etc.
•
In the Learning Center, you can view documentation, manuals, videos, guides, etc.


3.2.2 Introduction of main interface
Open the example project or new project provided by the official and enter the main interface, as shown in the
following figure:

(1) In the Project Summary interface on the right, you can see the project location, chip model, language,
comprehensive results, behavior results, etc.

After synthesis or behavior or Bit generation process, at the bottom of the interface, you can view Ultilization
(resource usage), Timing (wiring delay), and Power (power consumption).

(2) The Results Windows Area at the bottom is composed of five parts: Tcl Console, Messages, Log, Reports, and
Design Runs.

• Tcl Console part, you can run Tcl command, check Tcl message in the running process, etc. The operations
performed by the graphical interface (GUI) have corresponding Tcl command, which are usually displayed in the
Tcl Console. But many things that Tcl scripts can do, GUI method cannot handle, such as editing the synthesized
netlist

• The Messages part is used to identify the messages generated in the process of comprehensive simulation,
wiring, behavior verification, and Bit file generation, including Errors, Critical warning, Warning, Info, Status (identify
the specific IP core or the commands generated in the whole simulation routing process)

• The Log part covers the results of vivado analysis design and implementation design, such as RTL-level grammar
errors, DRC check errors, pin constraint errors, unreasonable path constraints, etc., but because the amount of
information in Log is too large, most of the important information is reflected through Messages. If an error is
reported during operation, and you cannot find it in Messages, you can check the Log information to
troubleshoot the error.

• The Reports section contains comprehensive results (size) reports for each module and IP. Double-click an item
(such as Place Design) to display resource utilization in the auxiliary view window.

• Design Runs part is used to view the comprehensive simulation, behavior results, the progress of bit file
generation, and the total number of resource usage, performance indicators, comprehensive time, integrated
version of IP, etc.
Note: For Vivado synthesis and other operations, the Elapsed in the Design Runs interface has not been
displayed, and an error is finally reported, which can reflect that the Vivado program is cut off in the
background or the library is incomplete, and the system needs to be re-installed to solve it.

(3)The Flow Navigator window on the left includes seven major parts such as Project Manager, IP INTERGRATOR,
simulation, RTL analysis, synthesis, mapping/behavior implementation,program and debug.
• The Project Manager part is composed of four parts: Settings, Add Sources, Language Templates, and IP
Catlog.

• The Settings section covers the entire Vivado IDE’s project compilation, tcl preprocessing commands, display style, project properties
and many other aspects.

• The AddSources part is similar to the "+" sign in the Sources window, is used to add or create constraint files, resource files, and
simulation files required by the project.

• Language Templates part is similar to Examples, as the writing examples of Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog, XDC, etc. provided by
Vivado.

• IP Catlog part, as the index window of IP core, can add IP core library address, IP core search, and IP core creation.

•
The main function of the IP INTERGRATOR part is to carry out embedded system design. The embedded system here includes
hard core and soft core, including Create Block Design, Open Block Design,Generate Block Design.

• Create Block Design, used to create a new block, open it and enter the graphical interface, add IP cores, and then design the
connection
• Open Block Design, used to open the existing block design, if it has not been created before, it cannot be opened
• Generate Block Design, used to synthesize the IP core used in Block Design.

The specific design steps are as follows:

◼The IP integrator is actually the XPS of the graphical interface version, drag in the soft core and IP core, and then
make the appropriate connection. The IP integrator provides the function of valid design to check whether there is a
problem with the connection.

◼The design of the embedded system through the IP integrator can be divided into the connection of the general
peripheral IP interface part of the system (hard core or soft core), self-built IP, and third-party IP custom data control
interface connection. The peripheral general IP of the system includes SPI, UART, I2C, DDR3, GPIO, etc. These IPs
usually use the AXI bus, and there are automatic wiring tools available in the IP integrator (run connection automation).
◼However, for third-party IP (such as ADI's peripheral chips and boards) and self-built IP, in addition to the control bus
AXI bus connected to the system, there are some additional control or data buses, which require DIY design and
manually wire the connection.

◼After finishing the layout and wiring of the graphics IP core, check the design.

◼After there is no problem, generate a vhdl or verilog shell file (with _wrapper suffix) from the .bd Block Design design
file to complete the embedding of an embedded system into the system project.

◼Finally, we need to develop the software project corresponding to the system, export the Block Design to the Xilinx
SDK (eclipse framework), and then develop the C project in the SDK.
•
The simulation part only contains Run Simulation. In simulation, you can select five parts such as behavioral simulation,
postsynthesis simulation,post-implementation timing simulation, post-implementation function simulation, and post-
implementation timing simulation.

• RTL behavioral simulation (functional simulation), as the first simulation executed in the design process. It is used to check
grammar errors in the code and the correctness of code behavior, but does not include delay information. If some special low-level
components related to the device are not instantiated, the simulation at this stage can also be done independently of the device. In the
initial stage of the design, no special low-level components can be used to improve the readability and maintainability of the code, and
the simulation efficiency can be improved, and it is easy to be reused.

• Post-synthesis function simulation (pre-simulation), as the second simulation executed in the design process. In addition to
outputting a standard netlist file, the synthesis tool can also output a Verilog or VHDL netlist. The standard netlist file is used to transmit
design data between various tools and cannot be used for simulation. The output Verilog or VHDL netlist can be used for simulation.
The reason why gate level simulation is called is that the simulation netlist given by the synthesis tool is already corresponding to the
underlying component model of the manufacturer's devices.

• Timing simulation (post-simulation), as the last simulation executed in the design process. After the design on the layout and
wiring is completed, a timing simulation model can be provided. The model includes device information and SDF timing annotation file
(Standard Delay format Timing Anotation) is provided.

• Register transfer level analysis (RTL analysis), only includes the Open Elaboration Design part. Describe the design in detail, you
can select the Report Methodology, Report DRC, check the RTL schematic.

• Report Methodology is to find current design error, generate report

• Report DRC is to report inspection results

• Check the RTL Schematic, open the schematic auxiliary view, and check the integrated results


• In the synthesis part, the RTL-level design description is converted into a gate-level description. In this process, logic optimization
will be performed and mapped to Xilinx device primitives (technology mapping). The device primitives refer to those gate-level primitives.
• The mapping/behavior implementation part maps the gates in the synthesized gate-level netlist to the CLB, connects the CLBs
according to the logical relationship, and performs layout and wiring as well as timing optimization.
• Program and debug part includes Generate Bitstream, opening JTAG device manager (Open Hardware Manager).

• Generate Bitstream, after clicking, it can automatically run synthesis, behavior implementation (layout and wiring, timing
optimization), and generate Bit.

• Open the JTAG Device Manager (Open Hardware Manager), after clicking, you can view the existing JTAG devices and the
FPGA chip connected to the JTAG, bit file download, Flash solidification, Debug (ILA)

(4) In the upper menu bar, there are File, Edit, Flow, Tools,Reports, Window, Layout, View , Help.

Here is a brief introduction to the use of Tools, as shown in the following figure:

•
Create and package new IP:

•
Create Interface Definition:
•
Enable partial reconfiguration：

•
Run tcl script：

•
Property editor：

•
Associate ELF files：

•
Generate memory Configuration file：

•
Compile simulation libraries：

•
Xilinx tcl store：

•
Custom commands：

•
Language templates：

•
Settings：


3.2.3 Introduction of simulation interface

Vivado simulator is a hardware description language event driven simulator. It supports function simulation and timing simulation, and
supports VHDL, Verilog, SystemVerilog and mixed language simulation.

(1) Click Run Simulation on the Flow Manager interface, and then select the simulation form (such as run behavioral simulation). The
toolbar will display the commonly used function buttons for controlling the simulation process, as shown in the following figure:

• 1.Restart: Re-run the simulation from time 0

• 2.Run All: Run the simulation until all events have been processed, or encounter an command to stop the simulation

• 3.Run For: Run the simulation according to the set time, and run the specified time for each point

• 4.Time: set step time

• 5.Step: Run the simulation until the next break-point state

• 6.Break/Stop: pause the simulation run

• 7.Relaunch Simulation: Recompile the simulation file and rerun the simulation. After the source code is modified and saved,
Relaunch is required to update the simulation

(2) In the Scope window, you can see the design structure. After selecting a scope, all signal objects in the scope will be displayed in
the Objects window. You can also select to add objects in the Object window to the waveform window to facilitate the observation of
internal signals in the design module.

For the display in the Scope window, you can set which types of scope to display in Settings. When a certain scope is closed and
displayed, all internal objects will be hidden.

By right-clicking a scope, the menu shown in the figure above pops up, and the specific explanation is as follows:

• Add to Wave Window: Add all objects whose status is visible to the waveform window. The value of the signal is displayed
from the moment when it is added to the simulation waveform. If you want to display the value before the insertion, you
must Restart or Relaunch (Relaunch will take more time )
• Log to Wave Database: You can select to record the object of the current scope, or record the object of the current scope and
all subordinate scopes. The relevant data will be stored in the wdb file in the project_name.sim/sim_1/behav directory.
•
Go to Source Code: Open the source code that defines the selected scope.

•
Go to Instantiation Source Code:Open the source code selected for instantiation (module for Verilog, entity for VHDL)

(3) In the Objects window, the signal objects contained in the currently selected scope are displayed. Signals of different types or
ports will be displayed with icons of different colors or shapes. The display type can be set in Settings.

By right-clicking the selected scope signal, you can make some settings:

• Add to Wave Window: Add the selected object to the waveform window display

• Radix: Set the display mode of the value of the selected object in the Objects window, including default, binary , octal,
hexadecimal, ASCII code, and unsigned decimal , signed decimal, signed magnuitude

Note: The setting here only changes the display mode of the object in the Objects window, and does not affect the display mode of
the waveform window

• Default Radix: Set the value represented by Default in Radix
• Show as Enumeration: Display the value of the SystemVerilog enumeration signal. When it is not selected, the value of the
enumeration object is displayed according to the setting mode of Radix
• Force Constant: Forcefully define the value of the selected object as a constant
• Force Clock: Forcefully set the selected object to a value that oscillates back and forth
• Remove Force: Remove all Force settings of the selected object

(4) In the Wave window, after running the simulation, a waveform window (named untitled) will be automatically opened, which displays
the waveform configuration of the signal in the simulation top-level module by default. If you close the waveform window by mistake,
you can click Window->Waveform to reopen it.

For the waveform configuration in the window (including signals, grouping conditions, display settings, etc.), it can be saved as a wcfg
file, and there is no need to re-add simulation signals and groups when the simulation is run next time.


In the waveform window, there are functions such as cursors, markers, and time rulers for auxiliary observation. By right-clicking the
selected signal, you can make some settings:


• Show in Wave Window: Highlight the selected object in the Object window

• Find/Find Value: The former is to search for an object, and the latter is to search for a value in the object

• Ungroup: Split group or virtual bus

• Rename/Name: The former sets the user-defined object display name, and the latter displays the selected name: long
(display the hierarchy), short (display only the signal name)
• custom(Rename set name)

• Waveform Style: Set the waveform display as digital or analog

• Signal Color: Set the display color of the waveform

• Divider Color: Set the color of the isolation band

• Reverse Bit Order: Reverse the display order of the numerical bits of the selected object

• New Virtual Bus: Combine the bits of the selected object into a new logical vector

• New Group: Add selected objects to a group, which can be arranged like folders

• New Divider: Add an isolation band in the waveform window to separate the signal for easy observation.

procedure:
4. Introduction of FPGA Development Program

4.1 Verilog development

4.1.1 Verilog grammar module

For the Verilog description language, each .v file needs a module, and the corresponding verilog module has different levels of
abstraction:

• 1. System level

• 2. Algorithm level

• 3.RTL level

• 4. Gate level

• 5. Switch level


Where, 1, 2, 3 belong to the behavioral description, 4 is the front end, and 5 is the back end

For the definition of a module, the keywords module and endmodule need to be used. These two appear in pairs and are
indispensable.

For example:
module
module_name( input
i_signal_name,
output
o_signal_name
);

endmodule

4.1.2 Execution block of Verilog grammar

(1) Sequential execution block（begin-end）：

begin

statement 1;

statement 2;

….
statement n;
end

It has the following features:
• The statement in the block are executed in order, and the next statement can only be executed after the previous statement is
executed.
• The delay time of each statement is relative to the simulation time of the previous statement.
• The program flow control will not jump out of the statement block until the last statement is executed.

In the begin-end statement block, the begin-end and fork-join blocks can be nested within each other or themselves. If the begin-
end contains a local declaration, it must be named (it must have a sign).
2) For the parallel execution block (fork-join):

fork

statement 1;

statement 2;

….

statement n;

join

It has the following features:
• The statements in the block are executed simultaneously, i.e, when the program flow control enters the block, the
statements in the block begin to be executed in parallel at the same time.
• The delay time of each statement in the block is relative to the time when the program flow enters the block.
• Delay time is used to provide execution timing for assignment statement.
• When sorted by time, the last statement is executed, or a disable statement is executed, the program flow control jumps out
of this module.

4.1.3 Delay expression of Verilog grammar
For the delay expression (#), the number after # represents the number of delay unit time, which can be a number directly or a variable
defined by a macro. The time unit of the delay is taken from the beginning of the .v file. For the use of the `timescale statement, for
example:
`timescale 1ns/1ps
Where, 1ns represents the minimum time unit, and 1ps represents the accuracy of the time unit.
An example of using a delay expression, such as: #10; represents a delay of 10 time units. If the `timescale statement is missing in
the .v file, the default time unit is 1ns.

4.1.4 Event expression of Verilog grammar
For the event expression (event), it can only be used for simulation. The signal in the testbench can be monitored to meet the event
trigger condition and trigger the corresponding processing.
The event in Verilog can only be used for simulation and cannot be synthesized. Examples of usage are as follows:



//Define an event

event reset_signal;
//The event is triggered after 10 time units
#10 ->reset_signal;
//Operation triggered by the event
@(reset_signal);


4.1.5 If conditional statement of Verilog grammar
For the if statement, it must be used in the process block (initial, always guided execution statement set),
For example：
always@(*)begin

if(statement 1)begin

Execute x0;

end

else if(statement 2)begin

Execute x1;

end

else begin

Execute x2;

end

end

Note: Provided the if statement is incomplete (cannot include all cases), the missing part will automatically compensate
the latch (the value remains unchanged)

4.1.6 Case conditional statement of Verilog grammar

For the case statement, it must be used in the process block (initial, always guided execution statement set),

For example:

always@(*)begin

case (expression)
Branch expression 1: statement 1;
Branch expression 2: statement 2;
Branch expression 3: statement 3;
default： statement 4;
endcase

end

In addition, there are two conditional statements, casez and casex, which are extended based on the case statement, which are
described as follows:

• The branch expression of casez statement does not consider the high resistance value z when comparing with the expression
• The branch expression of casex statement does not consider the high resistance value z and indefinite value x when
comparing with expression

Take casez as an example, as follows:

always @(*)
begin casez
(in[3:0])
4'bzzz1: out = 0; // in[3:1] can be
anything 4'bzz1z: out = 1;
4'bz1zz: out =
2; 4'b1???: out
= 3;
default: out =
0; endcase
end

Note:
■
casex is similar to casez.

The question mark? is a synonym for z, so 2'bz0 and 2'b?0 are the same.

4.1.7 While loop statement of Verilog grammar

For the while loop statement, a conditional loop (only used in the execution block) is implemented. The loop body will be executed
repeatedly only when the specified loop condition is true. If the expression condition is not true at the beginning (including false, X , Z),
then it will never be executed. Examples of statements are as follows:

always@(*)begin

while(loop condition expression)begin

Statement block

end

end

4.1.8 For loop statement of Verilog grammar

For the for loop statement, it must be used in the execution block. The structure example is as follows:
initial begin

for(expression 1; expression 2; expression 3)begin

statement block

end

end

The use of for statement in hardware description language is quite different from software description languages such as C language.
In Verilog, in addition to the use of for loop statements in Testbench (simulation test stimulus), the use of for loop statement in RTL-
level program is minimized.

The main reason: the for loop will be expanded by the synthesizer to execute statements for all variables. Each variable independently
occupies register resources. Each execution statement cannot effectively reuse hardware logic resources, resulting in a huge waste of
resources.

4.1.9 Forever loop statement of Verilog grammar

Forever loop statements are often used to generate periodic waveform, which are used as simulation test signals and must be written
in the initial execution block. Examples are as follows:


initial begin

forever begin

statement block

end

end

4.1.10 Repeat loop statement of Verilog grammar

For a repeat loop statement, it executes the specified number of loops. If the value of the loop count expression is uncertain, i.e, when
it is x or z, the number of loops is treated as 0. Examples of usage are as follows:

Repeat (repetition number expression) begin

statement block

end

Note:

• Loop number expression" is used to specify the number of loop, which can be an integer, variable or numeric
expression.

• If it is a variable or numerical expression, its value is calculated only in the first loop, so that the number of loop can
be determined in advance.

• A statement block is a loop body that is repeatedly executed.

• In synthesizable design, the loop number expression must remain unchanged (constant) during program compilation.
4.1.11 Structure description statement of Verilog grammar

(1) Initial statement is only a statement that is executed once, which can be synthesized, but only executed once. Unless the power is
turned off and restarted, the program reset is useless

(2) Always statement, always executed, conditional statements, loop statements, etc. can be set in the execution block

(3) Task statement provides a task structure that can take parameters and a non-zero continuation time. The task is to pass the result
through the parameters.

(4) Function statement, keyword declaration with parameters, is similar to the function in C language, and can only be used in the
execution block. Function is to pass the result through the return value.

4.1.12 System functions of Verilog grammar

System functions, most of which can only be used for simulation and cannot be synthesized

(1) Standard output functions: display and write

(2) Simulation monitoring: monitor

(3) End of simulation: finish and stop

(4) Time function: time and realtime

(5) File and memory processing: fopen, readmemh

(6) Random function: random

4.1.13 System pre-compilation of Verilog grammar

(1) Macro definition: `define

(2) File includes: ʻinclude

(3) Conditional compilation: ʻifdef, ʻelse, ʻendif

(4) Time indicator: `timescale

(5) Working library definition: ʻuselib
